chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who freed his slave-girl and made her manumission her dowry, then divorced her before consummating the marriage with her.

He said: He should seek her consent for half of her value; if she refuses, then she has one day of service and he has one day of service. And he said: And if she has a child, he pays for her half of her value and she is freed.

key_terms.أُمّ الْوَلَد: Mother of the child (implied by context of having a child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man frees his slave-girl as her dowry and divorces her before consummation?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies the specific legal status of a slave-girl whose manumission is treated as her dowry, a scenario distinct from standard free-woman divorces. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that if the man divorces her before consummation, he owes half her value as compensation, with an alternative of shared service days if she refuses payment. The presence of offspring triggers full manumission upon payment, highlighting the intersection of property rights, marital contracts, and lineage in Shia jurisprudence.
